text: The saying of old Antigonus was better, who, when he was to fight at Andros, and one told him, "The enemy's ships are more than ours;" replied, "For how many then wilt thou reckon me?" intimating that a brave and experienced commander is to be highly valued, one of the first duties of whose office indeed it is to save him on whose safety depends that of others.
author: Plutarch
speaker: Antigonus
translation: John Dryden et al., rev. Arthur Hugh Clough, 1864
